question.text: This company, based in Amsterdam, was given a monopoly on Dutch spice trade in 1602 and was one of the first major international corporations.
question.answerHtml: Dutch East India Company [accept United East Indian Company]
question.clue: It exported pepper from the Malukus, but was unable to displace Portuguese sandalwood traders from Timor.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the history of the Netherlands, whose name literally means "low-lying countries"
swap.text: Part of the modern-day Netherlands gained independence from the Spanish Empire in a war named for this many years, which is how long it lasted.

question.leadin: Answer the following about territorial exclaves in Europe.
question.text: Belgium has multiple enclaves and exclaves in the town of Baarle in this country, which resulted from a twelfth-century land exchange between the Duke of Brabant and the Lord of Breda.
question.clue: A woman born in this country agreed to a plot to seduce Crown Prince Wilhelm after her lover, a Russian pilot, was shot down in 1916.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about people who were murdered while praying.
swap.text: A count from this region was killed by the Erembald family while praying. This region contains the cities of Bruges and Antwerp and combines with Wallonia to form a country.
swap.clue: A shibboleth was used here prior to the Battle of the Golden Spurs, and parts of the "race to the sea" occurred here, ending after the opening of the sea-locks during the Battle of the Yser.

question.leadin: Answer the following about regions in Europe whose names derive from the old Germanic word for "foreigner,"
question.text: This culturally-divided country consists of the mainly French-speaking Wallonia to the south and Flanders to the north.
question.clue: This country's king surrendered it during World War II against the wishes of Pierlot, its prime minister.

swap.leadin: Sea Beggars were used by one side during this conflict.
swap.text: Name this conflict which saw William the Silent and Maurice of Nassau fight the Duke of Alba for control of a certain country.
swap.clue: Italian engineer Frederico Giambelli helped design fire ships during this war, during which Balthasar Gerard assassinated a leader.

question.leadin: In September of 1944, over 40,000 allied paratroopers were dropped near Arnhem in the Netherlands in an ambitious plan to end World War 2 by Christmas.
question.text: Name this failed operation. Its success depended on the taking and holding of several bridges.
question.clue: It was the last attempt to win the war by Christmas and had a strategic objective of forcing a crossing of the at .

swap.text: Attendants of the opera The Mute Girl of Portici joined in riots that led to the independence of this nation. This country's Leopold II created a brutal military force called the Force Publique.
swap.clue: One-third of the votes cast in an election in this country set up by the provisional government of Charles Rogier were left blank in protest.

question.text: This Flemish city saw half of its population flee in 1585 when the brutal "Spanish Fury" looted its besieged buildings and killed thousands of residents.
question.clue: Echoing Rome, the people of this city affixed the letters SPQA to its pioneering Beurs building.

swap.leadin: Identify the following about the violent history of Europe.
swap.text: Organized by the Duke of Alba, this court in the Spanish Netherlands attempted to suppress Calvinism and tighten Spanish control over the Netherlands by enforcing the Tenth Penny tax.
swap.answerHtml: Council of Blood [or Council of Troubles; or Raad Van Beroerten; or Bloedraad; or Tribunal de los Revoltosos; or Tribunal de Sangre; accept reasonable equivalents for "Council", such as "Court" ]
swap.clue: This tribunal created by the Duke of Alba to deal with unrest in the early stages of the Dutch Revolt.

question.leadin: This man rose to prominence in the service of Margaret of Parma, and he was almost assassinated by Juan de Jauregui for his support of independence.
question.text: Name this Stadtholder who was assassinated by Balthasar Gerard in 1584 after leading the Dutch Revolt.
question.clue: This leader's main antagonist dubbed this person a "pest on the whole of Christianity" and offered a massive bounty on this person's head, which led to the first assassination of a head of state with a firearm.

swap.text: This son of William the Silent was a stadtholder and an important strategist during the Dutch revolt. This protege of Oldenbarnevelt successfully besieged Breda.
swap.clue: This man used the alleged crime of raising of waargelder forces as an excuse to execute his the pro-Arminianism and pro-peace rival Johan van Oldenbarnevelt.

question.text: Many Flemish nationalists point to this battle during Philip IV's invasion of Flanders as a point of pride. Robert D'Artois ("dar-TWAH") was killed in this 1302 battle, named for a piece of equipment that was found littered on the battlefield after.
question.answerHtml: Battle of the Golden Spurs [or Battle of Courtrai]
question.clue: Stories of folk heroes who fought in this battle, such as the Cistercian lay brother Willem van Saeftinghe ("VILL-uhm vahn SAHF-ting-uh") and the weaver Pieter de Coninck, are romanticized in a novel by Hendrik Conscience ("kon-s'YAWNSS").

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the Netherlands before independence.
swap.text: Stadtholders were often members of this house. Members of this house included William the Silent, leader at the onset of the Dutch Revolt, and William III, who ascended to the throne of England in the Glorious Revolution.
swap.clue: That member of this house was killed at the hands of French Catholic Balthesar Gerard in one of the first assassinations by firearm, and led several early raids during the Eighty Years' War, during that "silent" leader served as stadtholder.

question.leadin: Identify each of the following about early American colonialization FTPE.
question.text: Chartered by the States General under Willem Usselinx, it had immediate control of New Netherland.
question.clue: This organization, whose leaders, the Heeren XIX ("nineteen"), developed the "Great Design." Later on, this organization authored the Charter of Freedoms and Exemptions in order to settle one colony through patroonships.

swap.text: This Dutch Admiral active during the Franco- and Anglo-Dutch wars commanded at the Four Days' and St. James's Day battles before destroying the docked British fleet in the daring Raid on the Medway.
swap.clue: He became friends with Frederick III of Denmark after relieving a Swedish siege of Danzig without fighting.

question.text: Ludvigsen was influenced by the Provo movement, which passed urbanist "White Plans" in this non-Danish city. This city's own squatters movement was involved in its 1980 coronation riots.
question.clue: Princess Beatrix's 1966 marriage to a German noble was protested in this city due to his previous membership in Hitler Youth.

swap.leadin: This event began when attendees of Daniel Auber's opera La Muette de Portici joined Catholic rioters outside the theater doors after hearing the duet "Sacred Love of the Fatherland."
swap.text: Name this 1830 event led by Charles Rogier ("roh-zhee-AY"). The Ten Days' Campaign supported by William I failed to topple a monarch installed during this event.
swap.answerHtml: Belgian Revolution [or Révolution Belge; or Belgische Revolutie; or Belgische Opstand; or Belgische Omwenteling; prompt on Belgian independence]
swap.clue: Sparked by perceived anti-Catholic policies, it brought to power the widower of Princess Charlotte of Wales, who later arranged the marriage of his niece Victoria to his nephew Albert.

question.leadin: Name these early explorers of Australia, FTPE.
question.text: This Dutch Navigator and colonial governor became the first European to sight the coast of Australia in 1606.

swap.text: The Dutch were led by this Grand Pensionary whose brother Cornelis accompanied the fleet at Medway.
swap.clue: In order to focus on his country's invasion in the War of Devolution, this man quickly negotiated the Treaty of Breda to end a war with England.
